name: VS Code / IDE AI agents
description: AI coding assistants and agents that run inside an editor or IDE (VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Trae, Kiro, etc.).

name: Terminal / CLI coding agents
description: AI agents controlled from a terminal or command line. Many can read a repository, edit files, and execute commands.

name: Open-source / BYOK / local AI tools
description: Tools distinguished by open-source licensing, bring-your-own-key model access, and/or local-model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) support. These attributes overlap heavily with categories A and B and are tracked per-tool in tools.yaml, not as separate products.

name: Autonomous software-engineering agents
description: Agents designed to work on a task end-to-end with minimal human intervention: plan, edit, test, iterate, and produce a pull request.

name: AI app / UI / full-stack builders
description: Hosted products that generate, deploy, and iterate on applications from natural-language prompts. Different from editor agents: the whole app lifecycle (build + host + database) is typically inside one product.

name: Documentation generation / platform tools
description: Documentation generators, AI documentation assistants, documentation platforms, API reference platforms, and developer portals.
